original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: For the fixed certified matching of 112 selected ports into 56 orthogonal two-port planes, can a joint four-message subset-sum decoder mix any two planes through an invertible 4x4 binary encoder and reduce the exact F2 pairing-rank copy invoice?
scope_change_reason: The card's two-unpaid-coordinate idea is tested at a concrete interface where two matched planes are jointly decoded. Existing paired-plane work leaves shared fractional scalar decoders open, while a complete coverage-law replacement would require a new endpoint contract and priced implementation. This bounded exact screen tests a binary-basis subfamily of that open decoder question without claiming a template change or construction.
bottleneck_link: The proposed extra unpaid coordinates would have to be realized by a cheaper multi-output decoder. This screen prices the exact pairing-rank charge of four joint messages across two already matched planes and asks whether basis mixing lowers the baseline invoice.
stop_rule: Enumerate every invertible 4x4 {0,1} encoder over Q, quotient by its exact source/reader support pattern, and test every unordered pair of the 56 certified planes. Stop after this four-message, two-plane binary-basis subfamily; do not infer a bound for general rational/complex encoders, overcomplete decoders, three or more planes, changed native primitives or physical routing.
evidence: The exact replay checks all 22,560 invertible binary matrices, 391 distinct support patterns and all 1,540 plane pairs (602,140 pair-pattern cases). Every pair has minimum copy cost 8, equal to two independent rank-two plane messages; there are zero strict improvements. RESULT.json binds the selected payload, matching certificate, source archive and per-pair minima digest. No selected kappa changes.
author: Gonzalo Mier, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research framing, exact enumeration, verifier implementation, validation and writing; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can a joint two-plane decoder with arbitrary rational coefficients, or with more than four scalar messages, lower the same pairing-rank invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The negative result only excludes binary four-message bases. A cheaper decoder outside that family could realize the unpaid-coordinate idea left open by the paired-plane interface work.
open_questions.first_step: Formulate a finite rational/linear-program relaxation for a fixed plane pair and prove that its objective equals or lower-bounds the native copy invoice; first screen the 1,540 fixed pairs before widening the port count.
open_questions.blocked_by: The basis screen supplies no completeness theorem for rational or overcomplete factorizations, and a relaxed algebraic factorization still needs a priced native interface and restoration schedule.

submission_checkpoint.decision: Continue the bounded two-plane decoder screen. Current priority guidance and pinned scientific inputs remain at revision 6; do not expand the construction family based on this local invoice result.
